headline: Highest risk is B data leakage: Prefect’s broad network egress can transmit workflow metadata if paired with a content-writing agent that produces untrusted instructions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a content-writing/open-source repo with no runnable I/O surfaces, while Prefect is an orchestration tool. A direct injection path is not documented, so the main plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or shared artifacts. That makes hijack risk possible but limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies agent_a-generated text into agent_b task definitions or prompts, injection content can propagate.
IF a shared file or message queue is introduced between the agents, attacker-controlled text can be reinterpreted as instructions.
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of agent_b prompt fields.
Use a fixed template that strips markdown and code fences before handoff.
Review any copied text for imperative instructions before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to handoff artifacts.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents with separate workspaces and no shared clipboard.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a is a content-writing repo with no declared data classes; agent_b has broad network egress and calls external APIs. If agent_a outputs workflow metadata or sensitive text into agent_b inputs, Prefect can transmit that context outward. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default orchestration use, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a is given sensitive source text and agent_b forwards task context to external APIs, that text can leave the local environment.
IF both agents share a workspace containing secrets, agent_b may upload or relay those contents through network egress.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared handoff files.
Disable outbound network access for agent_b on sensitive runs.
Redact inputs before passing them from agent_a to agent_b.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.
requires-engineering: add egress allowlists and content scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_a exposes no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Agent_b has broad network egress, but no filesystem or git write surface is shown. Overlap is therefore limited and any conflict would require extra, undocumented configuration.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external resource, conflicts can occur.
IF a shared mutable workspace is added later, concurrent edits may race.
mitigations: Avoid giving both agents write access to the same target.
Separate credentials and API tokens per agent.
Run one agent at a time for shared resources.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable state.
requires-engineering: introduce optimistic concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect is an orchestration/data-engineering tool that can act on upstream outputs, while the content-writing repo can generate persuasive but unverified text. If agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream workflow actions. No verification step is documented here, so the pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without validation, incorrect instructions can be executed downstream.
IF agent_a produces fabricated facts or citations, agent_b may propagate them into workflows or reports.
mitigations: Require human review before execution.
Add schema validation to agent_a outputs.
Compare outputs against a trusted source before acting.
requires-engineering: insert a verification gate between agents.
requires-engineering: log and alert on high-impact downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. Agent_b touches workflow metadata and has broad egress, while agent_a is a non-runnable content-writing repo with no data classes. Compliance risk is therefore limited to generic handling gaps rather than a concrete policy conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into agent_b workflows, outbound handling must match the governing policy.
IF retention or deletion requirements are imposed on workflow metadata, both agents must honor them.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair.
Document retention for workflow metadata.
Review outbound destinations for agent_b.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows.
